intents.intent: Live context is split by scope: 01-hot.md is a cross-project spine with a hard 2,500-character body budget carrying one line per project plus cross-project decisions, while each project's live state lives in its own 00-brief.md under a '## Now' section (state / next / open gates, 1,200 characters) that is rewritten in place — the dated decision lines below it keep the history. The reason, worth stating: a session then pays context only for the project it actually opens, so the auto-loaded cache stays flat no matter how many projects pile up.

In 00-index.md, update the 01-hot line in 'System files' to describe it as the spine plus a pointer to '## Now'. In AGENTS.md, do the same for its numbered read list and the project-brief line. Preserve any wording the user has already customized — add the behavior where it is absent, adjust in place where a stale description contradicts it; never rewrite a section wholesale.
intents.verify: 03-conventions.md describes both the 01-hot character budget and the per-project '## Now' section; 00-index.md and AGENTS.md both point a reader at '## Now' for a project's live state.

intents.intent: Every turn that has anything to report ends with a fixed block, last, after all other text: a horizontal rule, then '**⛳ BOTTOM LINE**', then the lines '✅ Done:' (what actually happened, at most two lines, no jargon), '⚠️ DECIDE:' (only when a decision is needed — the question plus a recommendation), '❓ OPEN:' (unanswered questions, batched, one line each), '▶ NEXT:' (what happens next or what is being waited on), and '📸' (a screenshot or file when the work is visual). Empty sections are omitted; a block with only Done and Next is the normal case. The rules that make it work: a needed decision may never live only in body text, everything above the block is optional reading, questions are batched into it rather than streamed mid-task, visual work ships a screenshot rather than a claim, and no jargon or file paths in the Done line. The point is that nothing important can hide in a wall of text.
intents.apply: Add this as a top-level '## Bottom Line — how every turn ends' section in CLAUDE.md, with the block shown in a fenced code example followed by the rules as bullets — written in the user's own first person, since CLAUDE.md is their file. In 06-usage-guide.md, add one bullet under 'Automatic — never ask for these' naming the block and saying it can be copied into the global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md to apply everywhere, or deleted if unwanted. In 03-conventions.md, add a short 'Reporting — the Bottom Line block' section pointing at CLAUDE.md as the definition. If the user has already written a reporting convention of their own, leave theirs in place and say so in the receipt rather than replacing it.
intents.verify: CLAUDE.md contains a Bottom Line section defining the ⛳ block with Done / DECIDE / OPEN / NEXT; the usage guide mentions it and how to opt out.
